title: Has a leap second ever been taken away?

scenes.purpose: Show the viewer the full span of the IERS record and that it only ever grows, one second at a time.

visual.description: Dark field; the IERS table of TAI-UTC values scrolls upward past the frame from 1972 to 2017, then settles into two large stat tiles side by side: 10 s / 1972 on the left, 37 s / 2017 on the right, with the intervening rows fading to a thin connecting line to show the steady climb.

chart.title: TAI-UTC, start to most recent value
chart.note: The table lists every value between these; each one is exactly one second more than the value before it. These tiles mark the endpoints, not the full run.

scenes.direction: Table of TAI-UTC values scrolls upward from 1972 to 2017, settling on the two highlighted stat tiles; hold half a second on the settled tiles before the cut.
scenes.narration: The IERS table of TAI-UTC runs from 10 seconds in 1972 to 37 seconds in 2017, each value exactly one second more than the one before it.

scenes.purpose: State the answer plainly: no leap second has ever been subtracted, only added.

visual.description: Hard cut to a dark field; a single title line types on in large serif: 'Only ever added. Never subtracted.' Hold on the settled line.

scenes.direction: Hard cut in; title types on; hold 1 s after the last word before the close card.
scenes.narration: No leap second has ever been subtracted from civil time; every one on record has only been added.
